**Deviation in piece 3.** You asked for the shared `record_id` grammar. `record_id` refuses `S2-CIT-E` (digit in the prefix), and the designer's case requires that id to pass. The engineer added a new shared definition `document_id` (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`) in `common.schema.json` for four of the types; `capability` uses `record_id`, which is unchanged. This is yours to accept or send back.

**Side effect in piece 3.** A missing shared field is now reported once instead of twice when the type's schema file is present; this applies to existing types too (the designer's case demands "the one finding").

## Packages

**P-1. Is a commit without trailers a violation of the `change` policy?**
- Why now: it decides whether `product-traceability-trailers` also declares `change`.
- Options: (a) no, trailers are traceability (CAP-13) and `change` is stated by `core-claims` only; (b) yes, add the pair with an evidence case.
- Impact: none on coverage today, `change` is covered either way.
- Reversibility and cost: one line in a declaration plus one case.
- Recommendation: (a), confidence medium. Built for (a); the exact-set case goes red if the pair is added without evidence.

**P-2. `human_gate` has no check (owner's, by DEC-613).**
- What the policy asks: the designer could not read the framework's per-key text (§20, under the archived sources). `docs/SOURCE_MAP.csv` line 154 ties §20 to "every policy key maps to a check" (DEC-046); the key maps to CAP-34 (decision packages and human gates).
- Where it is enforced today: in the orchestrator's process and the owner's chat, by packages and gates; no program holds it.
- Why no check qualifies: none of the twenty declared checks reads a gate or package record, so no planted violation can turn one red.
- It stays red (`policy-human_gate`, `POLICY_NOT_COVERED`) in every project. No recommendation from me beyond what DEC-613 fixes: it is not set to informational.

**P-3. The ticket schema and `depends_on` in record-id form.**
- Why now: `ticket.schema.json` allows only work-breakdown ids under `depends_on`. After the DEC-614 rewrite, W1-08's `test_the_committed_tickets_validate_against_the_ticket_schema` turns red.
- Options: (a) the schema accepts either form in this round; the designer's red case `test_w1_30_r15_depends_on_forms.py::test_the_ticket_schema_accepts_a_dependency_in_either_form_of_the_id` already holds it. (b) The schema changes in the commit that rewrites the tickets, and a designer removes that case.
- Impact: `gov check`'s core-schema does not read `depends_on` shapes, so only W1-08's case is affected.
- Reversibility and cost: one line in the schema (inside the ticket's `allowed_paths`); (a) needs one short engineer launch plus re-verification, (b) one designer launch.
- Recommendation: (a), confidence medium-high.
- Until decided, W1-30's suite holds this one failure.

**P-4. A dead argument across a path boundary.** `src/gov/ci/command.py` (outside the paths) still passes family names to `runner._check_policy_enforcement`, which now ignores them. Behaviour is correct. Recommendation: Wave 2 list.

## Policy keys

| Key | Declared by | Violation planted | Not caught by this check |

| security | `secrets-indexing` | canary `tier-form` in a packet under `.gov-runtime/` | secrets in tracked files, sensitivity classes, permissions |
| authority | `core-authority` | a ticket cites a research record under `sources` | who may approve; role limits on writes |
| test | `core-mutation` | an engineer ticket whose `allowed_paths` cover `tests/acceptance/` | failing or missing acceptance tests; an actual write |
| change | `core-claims` | last commit changes the readiness taxonomy with no change-execution record | any other governed file; any such record satisfies it |
| tool | `adapter-portability` | registry pins another rulesync version than the installed one | every other tool; installs; unregistered tools |
| context | `context-reproducibility` | a ticket names a source the store lacks | ceilings, superseded inputs, contradictions |
| checkpoint | `fresh-agent-reconstruction` | latest checkpoint has no `next_action` | no checkpoint at all (green); stale checkpoints |
| memory | `index-freshness` | a file committed after the index was built | retrieval quality, semantic index, record store |
